page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a decorative header ornament above the title. Margins hold only show-through and no printed notes, except one Greek word at the right of the first line. Bottom right: gathering signature.

main_text.head: THESES PHILOSOPHICÆ.
EX LOGICIS.
main_text.p: PHILOSOPHIA,σωφρόνως Pythagoræ ita dicta, cùm aliàs Sophia, seu Sapientia appellare-tur, vi nominis tantùm, non verò rei, amorem sapientiæ signi-ficat: Ejus objectum sunt res omnes quæ sub discursum evi-dentem cadere possunt; unde illam definimus habitum evidenter discurrendi de rebus omnibus. Itaque non satis accuratè definiri videtur per cognitionem rerum divina-rum & humanarum; vel per cognitionem rerum ut sunt: quia in ejusmodi definitionibus omittuntur, & genus Philo-sophiæ, & ejus differentia; genus quidem, cognitio enim, cùm sit nomen actus, non potest esse genus Philosophiæ quæ est habitus; differentia verò, quia nulla fit mentio evidentiæ discursus, quæ tamen est vera ejus

page.notes: The woodcut initial P is joined to "HILOSOPHIA" as "PHILOSOPHIA". The woodcut scene itself is not text. Faint mirrored text in the margins and at the top (including a faint running title and the word "nullum" at the foot) is show-through from the other side and is left out; no running head is clearly printed. The Greek word σωφρόνως is printed beside the first line, at the right. "THESIS I." is set as a paragraph because it is a numbered thesis. The text is cut off at the foot of the page and continues on the next page.
